# Killing a Hung Process on Linux

## Quick & Dirty (Most Common)

```bash
# 1. Find the process ID (PID)
ps aux | grep <process_name>
# or
pgrep <process_name>

# 2. Kill it
kill <PID>

# 3. If it ignores the polite kill, force it
kill -9 <PID>
```

## Step-by-Step

### 1. Find the Process
```bash
ps aux | grep firefox        # by name
ps -ef | grep <name>         # full command line
top                          # interactive (press k to kill)
htop                         # nicer top (press F9 to kill)
```

### 2. Kill It
```bash
kill 12345          # SIGTERM (graceful — lets the app clean up)
kill -9 12345       # SIGKILL (forceful — no cleanup, instant)
kill -15 12345      # Same as SIGTERM, just explicit
```

### 3. Kill by Name (without looking up PID)
```bash
pkill firefox       # SIGTERM
pkill -9 firefox    # SIGKILL
```

## If `kill -9` Doesn't Work

A truly hung process in **uninterruptible sleep** (state `D` in `ps`) is stuck in a kernel call (often disk I/O or NFS). You **cannot kill it** until the I/O completes or the device resets.

```bash
ps -eo pid,stat,cmd | grep ^.*D
```

Options:
- Wait for the I/O to timeout/complete
- Remount or reset the problematic
